Definition: a female slave (as a member of the household)
BiblicalUsage: Hagar comes to Abram's house as a maidservant, the firstborn of the maidservant behind the mill dies in the plague, the law gives the case of the bondmaid who is betrothed, and Moses warns that the people will be sold again as bondmen and bondwomen. The word is the woman of the household who owns nothing and can be given away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the maidservant is the Bible's test of how a household treats the powerless, because Hagar's story runs from Abram's tent to the wilderness and back. I hold that the God who heard Hagar hears every servant still, and I want my house to be one He would bless.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
